purpose: Select the change sites for removing Deno completely from this repository after the develop merge; only must_change and delete sites will be edited.

classes.description: The site must be edited for the target state to work: left as it is, a check, test, hook, build, installed environment or documented command would fail, or would run Deno where the target state runs Node or Turborepo, or would assume a per-package Python .venv or uv.lock. Examples: a new Deno.Command(...) call; a Deno.test(...) registration; Deno.execPath() spawned with 'run' or 'test'; a test asserting the text 'deno task backfire:install' in a message that the code changes; a deno.json task whose command must move to package.json or turbo.json; egg_base in a member pyproject; ready.py comparing sys.prefix with the package's own .venv; the commit-msg hook calling deno task commitlint. Takes precedence over can_stay when any part of the site must change. Excludes sites that only need deletion as a whole (use delete) and prose in historical records (use can_stay).

The site keeps working without an edit in the target state, or is outside the trial's scope. Examples: a Deno.readTextFile or Deno.env.get call that the @deno/shim-deno preload serves; import.meta.main; anything inside the shipped clean-code skill that stays on Deno; tools/spec-kit or tools/shellcheck paths; a test fixture string that merely contains the word deno as data and is not tied to a changed message; historical records in specs/ or .specify/. Does not apply when the site names a command, file or path that the target state removes or renames and a reader or check depends on it (use must_change).

The whole site becomes obsolete and should be removed rather than edited: a file or configuration entry whose job moves elsewhere. Examples: a per-package packages/<name>/uv.lock replaced by the root uv.lock; a deno.json top-level key such as nodeModulesDir or workspace whose job ends with the root deno.json; a .gitignore comment about Deno's cache. Use must_change instead when some of the site's content must be kept in a new form.

The evidence in the item is not enough to decide between the other classes, or the site is a governance or scope question that the user must decide (for example a sentence in AGENTS.md or the constitution naming deno task workflow).

batches.context:
Feature CHE-32 on branch feature/turborepo, now the real change (the user's decision of 2026-09-29), after merging develop 8ce9b2a. Target state:
- No Deno anywhere in the repository: no deno executable is required or invoked; no deno.json, deno.lock, plugins/code/deno.json or the clean-code skill's deno.json and deno.lock; no @deno/shim-deno and no Deno-API shim or preload (scripts/deno_shim.ts goes away and no command loads it); no Deno in the doctor, orca.yaml or the GitHub workflows.
- Every Deno.* call site in scripts/ and in the clean-code skill is rewritten to Node.js 24 built-ins: node:fs/promises and node:fs (readFile, writeFile, mkdir, rm, stat, lstat, mkdtemp, symlink, rename, readdir, copyFile, chmod, realpath, readlink, open), process (argv, env, exit, exitCode, cwd, chdir, kill, execPath, version, platform), node:child_process (already used where Deno.Command was), node:test, and Node types in place of Deno.FileInfo and similar. Deno.errors.NotFound checks become checks of the Node error code (ENOENT, EEXIST).
- @std/fs (walk, copy, exists, expandGlob, expandGlobSync, existsSync) calls the Deno global at runtime, so its imports are replaced with Node's fs (fs.glob or readdir with recursive, cp, existsSync). @std/path, @std/assert, @std/testing/mock, @cliffy/command, @eemeli/yaml and @zod/zod work on Node unchanged and stay.
- The clean-code skill runs on Node: it has its own package.json, package-lock.json and .npmrc; users run 'npm ci --prefix <skill-root>' once and then 'node <skill-root>/scripts/clean_code.ts'; its SKILL.md, the repository scripts that run it, and the copied-skill tests follow (decision D16).
- Tasks are root package.json scripts run by Turborepo; develop's Ruff checks (ruff check, ruff format --check, test:ruff) and its wiki-consistency:install change move into package.json and turbo.json; develop's new Deno tests (scripts/ruff_test.ts, the doctor's Ruff test) move to node:test.
- Python: one root uv workspace (unchanged decisions D6, D7, D10); the work plugin build must rewrite every workspace source of the copied wiki-consistency project, now including backfire; Ruff findings in the code the change added must be fixed.
- AGENTS.md and the constitution get the governance wording in a separate step (not code sites). Historical records in specs/ and .specify/ stay unchanged. Words such as 'Deno' in test names, comments or messages that describe behavior that no longer exists are must_change; mentions of Deno as history or of the removed tool in records are can_stay.

Feature CHE-32 on branch feature/turborepo, now the real change (the user's decision of 2026-09-29), after merging develop 8ce9b2a. Target state:
- No Deno anywhere in the repository: no deno executable is required or invoked; no deno.json, deno.lock, plugins/code/deno.json or the clean-code skill's deno.json and deno.lock; no @deno/shim-deno and no Deno-API shim or preload (scripts/deno_shim.ts goes away and no command loads it); no Deno in the doctor, orca.yaml or the GitHub workflows.
- Every Deno.* call site in scripts/ and in the clean-code skill is rewritten to Node.js 24 built-ins: node:fs/promises and node:fs (readFile, writeFile, mkdir, rm, stat, lstat, mkdtemp, symlink, rename, readdir, copyFile, chmod, realpath, readlink, open), process (argv, env, exit, exitCode, cwd, chdir, kill, execPath, version, platform), node:child_process (already used where Deno.Command was), node:test, and Node types in place of Deno.FileInfo and similar. Deno.errors.NotFound checks become checks of the Node error code (ENOENT, EEXIST).
- @std/fs (walk, copy, exists, expandGlob, expandGlobSync, existsSync) calls the Deno global at runtime, so its imports are replaced with Node's fs (fs.glob or readdir with recursive, cp, existsSync). @std/path, @std/assert, @std/testing/mock, @cliffy/command, @eemeli/yaml and @zod/zod work on Node unchanged and stay.
- The clean-code skill runs on Node: it has its own package.json, package-lock.json and .npmrc; users run 'npm ci --prefix <skill-root>' once and then 'node <skill-root>/scripts/clean_code.ts'; its SKILL.md, the repository scripts that run it, and the copied-skill tests follow (decision D16).
- Tasks are root package.json scripts run by Turborepo; develop's Ruff checks (ruff check, ruff format --check, test:ruff) and its wiki-consistency:install change move into package.json and turbo.json; develop's new Deno tests (scripts/ruff_test.ts, the doctor's Ruff test) move to node:test.
- Python: one root uv workspace (unchanged decisions D6, D7, D10); the work plugin build must rewrite every workspace source of the copied wiki-consistency project, now including backfire; Ruff findings in the code the change added must be fixed.
- AGENTS.md and the constitution get the governance wording in a separate step (not code sites). Historical records in specs/ and .specify/ stay unchanged. Words such as 'Deno' in test names, comments or messages that describe behavior that no longer exists are must_change; mentions of Deno as history or of the removed tool in records are can_stay.
